stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: A core prediction of labor economics is that when the cost of workers rises relative to the cost of machines, firms shift toward machines wherever a task allows it. Economist Dana Okafor applied this reasoning to grocery chains in states that raised their minimum wages between 2015 and 2022. ______ she expected stores facing the steepest wage increases to be the first to install self-checkout lanes, and installation records later confirmed that pattern.
explanation: The first sentence states a principle: costlier workers push firms toward machines. The second says Okafor applied it to grocery chains. The blank sentence gives the expectation she arrived at by doing that. If you put 'so' in the blank, it reads naturally: she applied the principle, so she expected the hardest-hit stores to automate first. 'Hence' expresses that cause-and-result link.

A.why: You took the result of applying the principle for an example of it. The sentence doesn't show one more firm switching to machines. It reports the expectation Okafor drew from the principle, and that expectation follows from it.

C.why: You read a contrast that isn't there. Okafor's expectation agrees with the principle she applied, so nothing needs to be conceded or reversed.

D.why: You picked a time word that puts her expectation before the reasoning that produced it. Her expectation came after she applied the principle, not before.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Training at high altitude, where each breath delivers less oxygen, prompts the kidneys to release more erythropoietin, a hormone that signals bone marrow to produce red blood cells. After several weeks, an athlete's blood can carry measurably more oxygen than it did at sea level. ______ many endurance coaches schedule a block of altitude training about a month before a major race, timing the return to sea level so the extra red blood cells are still circulating on race day.
explanation: The first two sentences explain how altitude training works and what it does: more red blood cells and blood that carries more oxygen. The last sentence describes a coaching strategy built on that benefit. Coaches schedule altitude blocks because of the mechanism, so 'Consequently' is the right transition.

A.why: You treated the coaches' scheduling as an example of the mechanism. The coaches aren't one more case of the body making red blood cells. They're acting on that fact, so their schedule is a result, not an instance.

B.why: 'Admittedly' concedes a point before a reversal. The passage never turns against the benefit of altitude training. The coaches put it to use.

D.why: You may have been pulled in by the mention of sea level. The coaching strategy doesn't oppose the mechanism. It depends on it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Under Halvorsen's 1962 zoning code, every new apartment building had to provide two parking spaces per unit, a rule that could consume a third of a small lot. When city planners studied stalled housing proposals, they found that this requirement, not the price of land, was what made small infill buildings unprofitable. ______ the city council eliminated parking minimums near transit stations in 2019, and permits for small apartment buildings in those areas tripled within four years.
explanation: The first two sentences establish a constraint and a finding: parking minimums, not land prices, were blocking small buildings. The last sentence describes the council's response and what happened next. The council acted because of the planners' finding, so 'Accordingly' gives the right cause-and-result link.

B.why: You treated the council's decision as an example of the planners' finding. It isn't another case of parking rules blocking construction. It's the action taken because of that finding.

C.why: You may have reacted to 'not the price of land' and expected a reversal. Repealing the rule doesn't defy the finding. It follows from it.

D.why: 'Likewise' signals a parallel point. The repeal isn't similar to the finding. It's what the city did in response.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: A radiosonde is a battery-powered instrument package that rises beneath a weather balloon, recording temperature, humidity, and pressure every second from launch until the balloon bursts roughly 30 kilometers up. Unlike a satellite, which infers these values from radiation it detects from orbit, a radiosonde directly measures the air it passes through. ______ it serves as the reference standard against which meteorologists check satellite temperature estimates.
explanation: The first two sentences describe what a radiosonde is: an instrument that measures the air directly instead of inferring values from a distance. The last sentence says what role it plays because of that, as the standard for checking satellite estimates. 'As such' fits because the sentence assigns the radiosonde a role as a direct result of what it was just described as.

A.why: You treated the radiosonde's role as an example of direct measurement. The last sentence doesn't give one more case of the radiosonde measuring air. It states the role that follows from measuring that way.

B.why: You carried over the contrast in 'Unlike a satellite.' The comparison has already been made inside the second sentence. The last sentence builds on it and doesn't reverse it.

C.why: 'Meanwhile' signals something happening at the same time or a separate thread. The reference-standard role isn't a separate event. It follows from how the radiosonde measures.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In 2023, ecologist Inés Paredes marked 60 frogs in Larch Pond, released them, and a week later captured 100 frogs, 15 of which carried her marks. In this mark-recapture method, the share of marked animals in a second sample reflects what fraction of the whole population the first sample represented. ______ Paredes estimated that the pond held about 400 frogs, since her 60 marked frogs appeared to make up 15 percent of its population.
explanation: The first sentence gives Paredes's data. The second gives the principle for interpreting it. The last sentence gives the estimate she reached by applying that principle to her data: 15 of 100 is 15 percent, and 60 is 15 percent of 400. Her estimate follows from the principle, so 'Thus' is correct.

A.why: You mistook the result of applying the principle for an example of it. Paredes's study was already the case under discussion. The last sentence isn't a new example. It's the conclusion her data and the principle lead to.

C.why: 'Still' signals that something holds despite what came before. Her estimate agrees with the method and her data. Nothing pushes against it.

D.why: 'Likewise' introduces a parallel point. The estimate isn't similar to the principle. It's the result of using it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Nickel-titanium alloys can be bent into almost any shape at room temperature, yet they spring back to a "remembered" form once warmed past a threshold set during manufacture. Engineers at a medical-device firm wanted a stent that could be folded small enough to pass through a narrow catheter and would then open on its own inside an artery. ______ they fixed the alloy's threshold at 33°C, a few degrees below body temperature, so that the stent would expand only after leaving the catheter.
explanation: The first sentence describes how the alloy works, and the second describes what the engineers needed. The blank sentence gives the design decision they made because of both, so you can put "so" in the blank and it reads naturally. "Thus" signals that result.

A.why: You treated the engineers' design choice as a sample of the alloy's behavior. Setting the threshold at 33°C is not one example from a larger group. It is what the engineers did because of the alloy's property and the stent's requirements, so it needs a cause-and-effect word.

C.why: "Still" signals that something happens despite what came before. Choosing a threshold below body temperature fits the engineers' goal. It does not go against it.

D.why: "Previously" places the action earlier in time, but the engineers could only choose a threshold after they knew what the stent had to do. The sentence follows from the need. It did not come before it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Concrete pavement grows and shrinks with the seasons: a 100-meter slab can lengthen by several centimeters between a January night and an August afternoon. Because concrete resists squeezing far better than it resists stretching, a slab poured as one unbroken sheet tends to crack wherever the pulling stress first exceeds its limited tensile strength. ______ road builders saw shallow grooves across fresh pavement every four or five meters, giving those cracks a straight, predictable place to form below the surface.
explanation: The passage first explains why unbroken concrete cracks unpredictably. The blank sentence describes what builders do in response: they cut grooves so the cracks form in planned places. The sawing is the result of the problem, so "Hence" is the logical transition.

A.why: You read the grooves as an example of concrete cracking. The grooves are not a case of the cracking. They are the builders' answer to it. When a sentence shows someone acting on a principle, it needs a cause-and-effect word, not an example word.

B.why: "Similarly" says the next sentence describes a parallel case. Sawing grooves is not another material behaving the way concrete does. It is what builders do because concrete behaves that way.

D.why: "Nonetheless" says the builders act in spite of the cracking. They cut the grooves because of the cracking, so a contrast word reverses the logic.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: How sharply a starchy food raises blood sugar depends not only on the starch it contains but also on how that starch has been handled. When cooked starch is cooled, some of its molecules realign into a tightly packed form that digestive enzymes struggle to break apart, and much of that form survives reheating. ______ a dietitian helping a patient avoid sharp after-meal spikes can reasonably suggest pasta that was cooked, refrigerated overnight, and warmed again over a freshly boiled batch.
explanation: The first two sentences state a principle: cooled starch becomes harder to digest and stays that way after reheating. The blank sentence gives the practical recommendation that follows from it. "So a dietitian can suggest..." reads naturally, and "As a result" expresses that link.

B.why: This is the subtype's trap. The sentence mentions a specific food, so it looks like an illustration. But it does not show starch realigning. It shows a dietitian using that fact to make a recommendation. Applying a principle is a result of the principle, not an example of it.

C.why: "In contrast" sets the sentence against what came before. The recommendation agrees with and depends on the starch findings, so nothing is being contrasted.

D.why: "Likewise" would introduce a second, parallel fact. The dietitian's advice is not another case like starch realignment. It is a conclusion drawn from it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Some vaccines train the immune system using a live but weakened virus, which provokes an especially strong and lasting defense. In people whose immunity is suppressed, however, such as transplant recipients taking anti-rejection drugs, a weakened virus can occasionally multiply unchecked and cause the very illness it was meant to prevent. ______ physicians give these patients an inactivated version of a vaccine whenever one exists, accepting a somewhat weaker response in exchange for removing that danger.
explanation: The previous sentence identifies a risk: live vaccines can cause illness in immunosuppressed patients. The blank sentence describes how physicians respond to that risk. You can put "because of that" in the blank, so "For this reason" is correct.

A.why: You took the physicians' practice as an example of a live virus multiplying unchecked. It is not an example of that danger. It is the precaution physicians take because the danger exists.

B.why: The phrase "accepting a somewhat weaker response" may have made the sentence sound like a concession, but "Even so" means the physicians act despite the risk. They switch vaccines because of the risk, so the relationship is cause and effect, not contrast.

C.why: "Meanwhile" marks something happening at the same time but separately. The physicians' choice is directly caused by the risk just described. It is not an unrelated event running alongside it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: When a crowded highway gains lanes, traffic researchers have found, the added space soon fills: drivers who once avoided the route or traveled at other hours begin using it, and within a few years delays are often as long as before. Officials in one fast-growing city weighed this pattern carefully while deciding how to relieve a jammed eight-kilometer corridor. ______ they set aside plans to widen the road and instead converted two existing lanes into a busway with buses arriving every four minutes.
explanation: The passage states a general finding (new lanes fill up again) and says the officials took it into account. The blank sentence reports the decision they reached because of it, which was to skip widening and build a busway. "Thus" marks that decision as the outcome of their reasoning.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. The busway decision is not an example of new lanes filling up. It is what the officials concluded after applying that finding. A finding reached by using a principle follows from the principle, so it takes a cause-and-effect word.

C.why: You may have read "set aside plans to widen" as a reversal. But dropping the widening plan agrees with the evidence that widening doesn't last. The officials followed the research instead of going against it.

D.why: "Similarly" would introduce a parallel case of the same pattern. Converting lanes to a busway is not another highway filling with traffic. It is a choice made because of that pattern.
